title: Disabling the Sensitivity Settings for DLP Engines

blocks.text: Data sensitivity determines how susceptible the data is along with the level of risk associated with it, which could lead to data breaches. For example, the sensitivity level is high for personally identifiable information (PII) or credit card numbers, moderate for email addresses, and low for data that does not have any sensitive or confidential information.

DSPM scans the data using the predefined DLP engines and dictionaries to detect and classify sensitive data and generates alerts. Only DLP engines assigned to the DSPM channel in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) are displayed on the Data Classification Settings page. To learn more, see Understanding DLP Engines and Dictionaries.

By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines. You can disable the sensitivity setting when you don't want the DLP engines to classify sensitive data. If you disable the sensitivity setting for all DLP engines, any new DLP engine that is added to Internet & SaaS is not automatically synced with DSPM. You need to manually enable the sensitivity settings for such DLP engines in the Zscaler Admin Console.
To disable the sensitivity setting for DLP engines:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Data Classification Settings.
In the Sensitive column, disable the toggle for the required DLP engine.
Read the confirmation message that appears, then click Disable.
